input: Formal audiometry was completed this week, and the signed audiologist report states that mean unaided threshold in the better ear was 47 dB, averaged over 500, 1000, 2000 and 3000 Hz.

The report explicitly confirms removal of both hearing aids during testing and identifies the better ear, so those measurements are distinguished from the driver's account of hearing reasonably well when his aids are working.

One aid intermittently stops working near the end of a shift, and the driver sometimes misses dispatch instructions in background noise; no current aided-performance assessment establishes whether the aids meet the relevant standard.
The optometrist confirms a visual field defect on a separate current signed assessment.

The driver is unsure whether a remote dizzy spell involved loss of awareness, so the number of confirmed events and the appropriate event-free interval remain unresolved despite documentation of the recent event and the visual field defect.
The driver had transient loss of consciousness while seated after a delivery, with a colleague documenting failure to respond and a brief gap in recall.
An emergency differential mentions arrhythmia and seizure without confirming either, and a glucose measurement obtained after food cannot establish the cause of the event.
The GP's separate current summary records that persistent blood pressure remains 182/108 mmHg after repeated measurements.
